items.title: fix: use relative import for table module in metrics.py
items.body:
## Problem
`schematiq-lib/schematiq/evaluation/metrics.py` used an absolute import (`from table import Table`) instead of a relative one, even though `table.py` lives in the same directory and the sibling `__init__.py` correctly uses `from .table import Table`.

This import only resolves if `evaluation/` itself happens to be on `sys.path` — which never happens under normal usage (importing `schematiq.evaluation`, running `test_evaluation.py` via pytest from repo root, from `schematiq-lib/`, or from `backend/`). Under all realistic import paths it raises `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'table'`.

## Solution
Changed the import to `from .table import Table`, matching the working pattern already used in `evaluation/__init__.py`.

## Verify
```
git apply --ignore-whitespace --check fix-metrics-table-import.patch
python -m py_compile schematiq-lib/schematiq/evaluation/metrics.py
( cd frontend && npx tsc --noEmit )
```
Confirmed via direct package-import test: before the fix, importing `schematiq.evaluation.metrics` as a package (the real-world usage pattern) raises `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'table'`; after the fix it imports cleanly.

## Changes

- Add an idempotent incremental migration that creates or repairs public.operational_metrics.
- Enable RLS, remove the obsolete admin policy, deny public/anon/authenticated access, and grant only SELECT and INSERT to service_role.

items.title: Fix table over-classification + thread measured metrics into table cells
items.body:
## The report

Overlay text rendering at roughly **25-40% of expected size**, placement off, and table structure not adhered to, in **both** the `/debug` A|B preview and the PDF outputs. Three coupled defects, all in the consumer-side synthesis/render layer. The byte-parity leaves are untouched.

## Root cause (measured, real 2550×3300 two-column scan)

`recognize_document_with_options` derives **two** things from `opts.strip_borders`, and the earlier ingredient-3 fix covered only the first:

1. **SPLITTING** — `rec_blocks` (`lstm_recognizer.rs:1201-1205`) and the classification `blocks` list (`:1241-1245`) — gated, as documented.
2. **LABELLING** — `table_blocks` (`:1269-1272`) mapped `block_is_table` over every block with **no gate at all**. That boolean is what `build_regions` stamps as `region.type`.

Result on the plain default path: **2 of 5 regions and 69 of 72 lines stamped `type=table`** on a page with *zero printed rules* (`nhb = nvb = 0`, scoring on `nvw` alone). Those lines then rendered through `TableCell`, which **had no metrics field at all** and whose two render call sites hardcoded `None` — so they fell to `box_h * 0.5` sizing and a box-**bottom** pen. `doc_probe`: measured `font_px` median **48.0** vs the fallback's **30.0** (0.53-0.67×), exactly the shrunk text reported.

## Fix 1 — narrow the *evidence*, don't switch detection off

**The plan's original design was rejected during implementation.** It proposed gating `table_blocks` behind `strip_borders`; that would have broken `naive_pre_strip_destroys_table_detection`'s precondition (`!plain_shapes.is_empty()` — *"or this test measures nothing"*) and discarded ruled-table detection that demonstrably works.

Only the **whitespace half** of `decide_if_table` is unreliable (`nvw>3`, `nvw>6` — wide multi-column TEXT produces the same long corridors a table does; `resgrid.pgm` is 8 columns of ordinary text scoring `nvw=17`). The **ruled half** (`nhb>1`, `nvb>2`) is sound. So the default path now *additionally* requires ruled evidence, while a `strip_borders` caller keeps the bare verdict — necessarily, since stripping **removes** the rules the ruled conditions count.

- `TableDecision::has_ruled_evidence()` — a pure read of counts `decide_if_table` already computes. **The byte-parity leaf is unchanged.**
- `pageseg::region_table_decision()` — returns the full decision; `region_is_table` now delegates to it so the two can never disagree.
- `block_is_table(..., require_ruled)`; call site passes `!opts.strip_borders`.

**Measured after: 5 regions, all `type=text`, 0 tables** (35+34+1+1+1 = 72 lines). Those lines now take the `TextBlock` path that already consumed measured metrics — so **Fix 1 alone resolves the reported symptom on this page**.

## Fix 2 — `TableCell` carries the metrics its own row already computed

A cell is by construction "one line's words in one column", so its typography *is* that line's typography. `structured::TableCell` gained `metrics`, `doc.v1` emits the same additive per-cell keys lines already carry, and the PDF/HTML renderers parse and use them at both call sites. The 3-tier size ladder is now **one shared `derive_text_metrics()`** used by the line and cell paths, so they cannot drift. This is what protects a *genuinely correct* table.

## Test plan

- [x] **339 tests pass** across `tesseract-ocr` / `tesseract-ocr-pdf` / `tesseract-ocr-web` (release), 0 failures
- [x] `cargo fmt` + `clippy -D warnings` clean on both touched crates
- [x] 8+7+0 CER fence re-verified **with its real numbers printed** (`0.000` ×14, `0.023`, `0.814`) — unchanged, as expected since recognition is upstream of classification
- [x] Goldens unchanged
- [x] New falsifiers, each verified against pre-fix code, all two-sided:
  - `require_ruled_rejects_rule_free_multi_column_text_that_scores_on_whitespace_alone`
  - `block_is_table_detects_grid_not_paragraph` (extended to run under **both** strictness settings)
  - `table_cell_uses_measured_metrics_not_the_box_fallback` (`Tf` must be 48 and must NOT be 30.5; pen on measured baseline, NOT box bottom; HTML matches)
  - `doc_v1_layout_parses_cell_metrics` (keys present → metrics; absent → `None`, proving the parse reads rather than fabricates)

The new fixture's `nhb`/`nvb` guards earned their keep: a first attempt with 6px marks measured `nvw = 1`, because `decide_if_table`'s own `o8.1` noise-clean **erased every mark**. Each constant is now chosen against a specific step of the chain.

## Also: `.claude/agents/` — the lessons written down

Seven cards encoding this session's troubleshooting: `parity-oracle-smith`, `measurement-skeptic`, `falsifier-auditor`, `heuristic-gate-warden`, `render-typography-engineer`, `subagent-output-auditor`, `transcode-scope-warden`, plus a README with the four rules that generalize. Each leads with the rule, then the **measured incident** that produced it, then a checklist — provenance is the point, since a rule without its incident gets ignored under pressure.

`subagent-output-auditor` exists because of a failure *in this session*: a verification workflow reported "completed, exit 0" while one agent returned schema-**valid** but content-**free** placeholder data and another died on a retry cap, surfaced only in the `<failures>` block.

items.title: fix(report): size the metrics table for winter, not for today
items.body:
Follow-up to #19, found by verifying it against the live page instead of the local preview.

### The one-pixel margin

#19 made three of four tables fit a 390 px viewport. On the published page the metrics table measured **337 px against 336 available** — it fitted, but with nothing to spare, and only because August's errors are single-digit.

Re-measured with the widest realistic content — two-digit MAE and RMSE, two-digit bias — that table came to **346 px and scrolled again**. The fix as shipped held only while the air was clean, and would have broken in the smog season this page exists for.

### What changed

`0.78rem` with 4 px padding (from `0.82rem`/5 px). The same winter case now measures a min-content **324 px against 336** — a 12 px margin.

| Table | min-content, winter figures | Available at 390 px | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Predictor | 324 | 336 | fits, +12 |
| Interval | 264 | 336 | fits, +72 |
| Hours (regimes) | 224 | 336 | fits, +112 |
| Lead | 360 | 336 | scrolls, by design |

### A measurement note

Rendered width is useless here: `table { width: 100% }` pins every table at exactly the card's 336 px whether it has room to spare or none at all — which is why #19's margin looked like `+0` for all three. The figures above come from forcing `width: min-content` per table and reading the box back.

The CSS comment now records the winter floor, the figure the previous setting produced, and that below ~380 px the margin is gone again. Suite stays at 448.

## What
The Recent Email Performance table and the per-recipient drill-down had columns drifting right of their headers — e.g. the `Sent` value rendered under the `Opens` header.

## Why
Flex text cells (`Subject`, `Date`, `Email`, `Ecclesia`, `Delivered`, `Status`) used `numberOfLines={1}` but no `minWidth={0}`. On web, flex items default to `min-width: auto` (content-based), so a long Subject/email refuses to shrink to its flex slot and pushes every following column right. The classic flexbox min-width trap.

## Fix
Add `minWidth={0}` to those cells so each respects its flex basis and truncates (ellipsis) instead of overflowing. Headers unchanged (short text, never overflowed).

several issues found while running them end-to-end against dev.

## Metrics: migrate to the metrics table

The `AnalysisDataType.metrics` download is deprecated; metrics now come from the
metrics table via `activity_metrics`.

- **`activity_analysis.py`, `session_data.py`** — when `metrics` is selected, fetch via
  `activity_metrics` and save a single flat JSON (`<slug>_metrics.json`) instead of the
  deprecated analysis-data download. Report and data files still download through
  `analysis_data_for_activity`. Adds a shared `_metrics_to_dict` helper (scalar →
  number, bilateral → `{"left", "right"}`).
- **`activity_metrics.py`** — scoped down to single-activity metrics only (dropped the
  `subject_metrics` demo). Flattens the grouped metrics to a `name → value` mapping and
  drops the `activity_type_id` display.

## OpenCap import (`opencap_import.py`)

Fixes for importing OpenCap sessions into a v2 backend:

- **v2 rejects direct trial `meta` updates** (`"Direct meta updates are not allowed."`),
  which caused a bare `HTTP 400` on the first trial carrying meta (e.g. calibration).
  The source trial `meta` is now stripped before `import_session`.
- **`coreengine` override was silently ignored.** The source `augmentermodel` was being
  re-applied over an explicit override (e.g. `v1.0` reverted to `v0.3`). The script now
  translates `augmentermodel → coreengine` up front so the override wins.
- **Drop `posemodel`** from the session meta — it is an OpenCap-only setting, unused in
  Model Health.
- **Remove the session-level framerate override.** Framerate is intrinsic to the recorded
  videos, so it is always taken from the source session and can no longer be overridden
  (removed the `framerate` key, `_FRAMERATE_MAP`, and `SessionFramerate` import).
- Example config tidy-up: `trial_meta_overrides` defaults to empty with clearer sample
  trial names.

## Recording (`activity_recording.py`)

- Re-fetch the activity before `update_activity`. Analysis auto-generates tags
  server-side, and `update_activity` merges add/remove tags on top of the local
  activity's tags — without a fresh fetch the merge started from a stale set and wiped
  the auto-generated tags.

## Docs (`README.md`)

- Added entries for `activity_metrics.py` and `update_activity.py`.

## Testing

- OpenCap import: reproduced the full import HTTP sequence against
  `dev.modelhealth.io/api/v2`. Confirmed the trial-meta patch is what returned 400, that
  stripping it lets the import proceed, and — via patch + read-back — that a
  `coreengine: "v1.0"` override is stored as `v1.0`, `posemodel` is absent, and the
  source `framerate` is preserved.

## Related

The underlying SDK fixes (skip raw meta patch on v2, `augmentermodel`/`coreengine`
precedence, drop `posemodel`) are in a separate `model-health-internal` PR. The example
changes here also work with the currently-shipped SDK ahead of that rebuild.

items.title: fix: refresh RDBMS table-row-count metrics asynchronously
items.body:
## Summary

`PhysicalTenantsRdbmsTableRowCountMetrics` exposes a Prometheus gauge per RDBMS table whose value supplier (`RdbmsTableRowCountProvider.getRowCount`) ran a synchronous, unbounded `COUNT(*)` query against the database on every scrape, cached for a fixed duration (default 15 min) via a plain Caffeine `expireAfterWrite` cache.

If the database becomes slow or unreachable, the *first* scrape after the cache entry expires blocks the scrape-handling thread indefinitely (no query timeout is configured for RDBMS anywhere in this codebase). Reproduced in a load test: after killing the backing Postgres instance, Prometheus metrics for the whole cluster silently stopped ~5 minutes later (matching the cache duration) even though the broker/engine kept running — because the scrape endpoint thread was stuck waiting on a dead connection.

- **Motivation**: this metrics endpoint should never be able to block on the database, regardless of DB health.
- **Fix**: switch `RdbmsTableRowCountProvider` to Caffeine's `refreshAfterWrite` + `buildAsync`, backed by a small bounded, dedicated executor. `getRowCount` now always returns immediately — either the last successfully loaded value, or `-1` if no load has completed yet (e.g. first call, or a load currently in flight) — while the (potentially slow/blocking) reload runs off-thread.
- The executor is shared across all physical tenants' providers and bounded to 2 threads, so even if every table's refresh across every tenant hangs simultaneously, this can never grow unbounded or starve the connection pool used by other read paths.

items.title: fix(metrics): set dropped database table size to 0 in Yabeda
items.body:
### 📝 Summary

Yabeda does not auto-clear tags from memory when they disappear. When a database table is dropped (e.g., during database migrations or Cyndi syncer table drops), its last-recorded size remains in the Prometheus exporter payload indefinitely.

To mitigate this, this PR:
1. **Isolates Collection:** Moves database metrics collection into `Compliance::TableSizeCollector.collect`.
2. **Handles Dropped Tables:** Diffs currently active PostgreSQL tables against Yabeda's registered keys. If a table is missing:
   * It explicitly **sets its size to `0`** so Grafana immediately drops the metric line to 0 (since multi-process `yabeda-prometheus-mmap` `.db` files on disk do not support dynamic key deletion).
   * It deletes the tag from the local Ruby VM memory as a best-effort cleanup.
3. **Improves Diagnostics & Process Checks:** Switches initializer Sidekiq/Karafka boot checks to use `$PROGRAM_NAME` and logs full backtraces with `Exception#full_message` on collection failures.
4. **Adds Unit Tests:** Adds a new, isolated RSpec suite in `spec/initializers/yabeda_spec.rb` utilizing `Faker` data and an `after` block registry teardown to prevent cross-spec pollution.

items.title: Fix BetterStack ClickHouse table naming; document metrics querying
items.body:
## Problem

The nori bug agent got stuck trying to query pgbouncer metrics from BetterStack — queries kept failing with "table doesn't exist" even though `SHOW TABLES` listed the source. Root cause: the agent cookbooks taught the ClickHouse collection pattern as **`t<SOURCE_ID>_<slug>_logs`**, using the per-source ID as the prefix.

That's wrong. The prefix is the **team ID `t455770`** — a workspace-wide constant that's the same for every table. The source ID never appears in a ClickHouse table name (it identifies a source in the Uptime API only). Using it is rejected with `CLUSTER_DOESNT_EXIST`.

Verified live against the ClickHouse endpoint:
- `remote(t455770_nori_render_logs)` → 159K rows ✅
- `remote(t1508391_nori_render_logs)` → `CLUSTER_DOESNT_EXIST` ❌

The same wrong table name was copy-pasted across all three agent cookbooks, so it was silently breaking **log** queries for every agent too — not just the bug agent's metrics.

Secondly, **metrics were never documented at all** — the cookbooks only covered the log-query shape (`SELECT raw ...`), so the agent had no way to reach pgbouncer / postgres slow-query / taskiq / llm metrics, which live in a separate `_metrics` table with a different (row-based) query model.

## Changes

- **Correct the table-naming rule** to `t<TEAM_ID>_<source_slug>_<signal>` across bug/support/eval-gate cookbooks + AGENTS.md, with an explicit source-ID-vs-team-ID warning callout.
- **Add a full Metrics subsection** to the bug-agent cookbook:
  - row-based query model (`WHERE name='...'`, `maxMerge(value_max)`/`avgMerge(value_avg)`, `label('...')` for tags)
  - verified pgbouncer + postgres slow-query metric catalog
  - copy-paste queries including a reproduction of the **PgBouncer max-wait alert** (`pgbouncer.pool.maxwait_seconds`, pool = `label('database')`)
  - note that times are UTC (ET = UTC−4)

All metric names, the `database` pool label, and the queries were verified against the live ClickHouse endpoint (incl. reproducing the actual incident: `nori_input` maxwait = 2s at 15:48 UTC / 11:48 ET).

## Note

These are the version-controlled docs. Running agents load `~/nori/nori-agent/data/API-COOKBOOK.md` on their own boxes and won't pick up the fix until re-synced from the repo.

## What
Tranche 4 (DynamoDb) maintainability quick wins. No behavioural change to request handling.

### #5 — KnownOperations metrics drift (real fix)
The operation-metrics allowlist (`KnownOperations`) was a hand-maintained **15-op** array that had silently drifted from:
- the **20** ops `HandleAsync` actually dispatches, and
- the **30** ops the wire parser (`DynamoDbOperationNames.Map`) recognises.

Since `IServiceModule.ExtractOperationName` collapses anything outside the allowlist to `"unknown"` (IServiceModule.cs:117), **five implemented ops** — `DescribeTimeToLive`, `UpdateTimeToLive`, `TagResource`, `UntagResource`, `ListTagsOfResource` — were being mislabelled `"unknown"` in metrics.

Fix: derive `KnownOperations` from `DynamoDbOperationNames.ShortNames` (the single wire-protocol op table), so the allowlist **can never drift again**. Every parseable op is now labelled by name; only unrecognised `X-Amz-Target` values collapse to `"unknown"` (cardinality stays bounded at the 30-entry table). Added `ExtractOperationName_labels_every_handled_op_by_name` regression theory + an `unknown` guard.

The doc-comment said the synthetic ARN includes the *Cosmos endpoint*, but the format is `arn:aws:dynamodb:azure:{accountId}:table/{name}` — account id, not endpoint. Corrected.

items.title: fix(prometheus): tolerate absent tables in namespaced metrics collection
items.body:
Release version:
6.1.5, 6.2.3, 6.3.0

## Summary

Fixes the product robustness issue flagged as out-of-scope in #18179: the Prometheus collector crash-loops with `{badarg, ets:first(emqx_mt_ns)}` on every scrape of the namespaced stats when the `emqx_mt` application is not running, because `emqx_mt_state:fold_known_nss/2` does not guard against its table being absent and `emqx_mt` is not a dependency of `emqx_prometheus`.

Guard at the source, so any caller is safe and the semantics stay correct (no namespaces / no records exist when the owning feature is not running):

* `emqx_mt_state:fold_known_nss/2` returns the accumulator unchanged when `emqx_mt_ns` does not exist.
* `emqx_mt_state:is_known_ns/1` returns `false` in the same situation (reached via `emqx_mt_state:count_clients/1` on the same collect path when a specific namespace is queried).
* `emqx_authz_mnesia:record_count_per_namespace/0` and `emqx_authn_mnesia:record_count_per_namespace/0` (the sibling authz/authn gatherers on the same collect path) return an empty map when their count tables are absent, i.e. when `emqx_auth_mnesia` is not running — it is not a dependency of `emqx_prometheus` either.

Tests: a new CT case scrapes `/prometheus/namespaced_stats` with `emqx_mt` and `emqx_auth_mnesia` not started and asserts a 200 response with the namespaced session/authz/authn metrics omitted; the existing `t_namespaced_stats` case now also asserts that `emqx_sessions_count` is still emitted per namespace when `emqx_mt` is running; eunit covers `fold_known_nss/2` and `is_known_ns/1` with the table absent.

items.title: Survive a missing metrics table instead of crashing (#30)
items.body:
Fixes #30.

ETS calls against a missing metrics table raise `ArgumentError` and crash the caller. The table is created in `Mobius.init/1` before consumers start, but a startup race or a restart of the table's owner can leave a consumer (telemetry handlers, `Scraper`, `Registry` reconciliation) with no backing table. `MetricsTable.init/1` could also crash the supervision tree on a duplicate named table (restart) or a failed dump restore.

Mobius is observability — it should degrade, not take down the host app.

**Fix** (`lib/mobius/metrics_table.ex`):
- Add `exists?/1` via `:ets.whereis/1`.
- Reads (`get_entries/1`, `get_entries_by_metric_name/2`) return `[]` when the table is absent.
- Writes (`put/5` and helpers) drop gracefully when the table is absent.
- `init/1` is idempotent: reuse an existing named table, and degrade a failed restore to a fresh table with a logged warning.

**Tests:** robustness coverage for an absent table — reads → `[]`, writes → `:ok`, idempotent `init/1`.

items.title: refactor(query): single op dispatch table; fix by-op metrics gap (#187)
items.body:
The operation set was enumerated in **four disconnected places** — `dispatch_inner`'s strcmp chain, `is_write_op`, `metric_op`, and `op_names[]` — with nothing keeping them in sync.

**The bug this exposed:** `forget`, `export`, `purge`, `consolidate`, and `history` were dispatched and policed as real ops but were absent from `metric_op`/`op_names`, so they silently bucketed into `by_op.other` — invisible in `stats` and the Grafana dashboard.

## Change
- **Normalize** every dispatch handler to one signature: `cJSON *(AegisDB*, const cJSON*, const AuthCtx*)`. Handlers that ignore `req`/`ctx` cast them `void`; the namespaced handlers read `ctx->ns`.
- **One `OpDef` table** (`name`, `fn`, `flags`, `metric`) is now the single source of truth. `dispatch_inner`, the auth/write policy (`OP_WRITE` / `OP_GLOBAL` / `OP_WRITE_TOK` / `OP_NOAUTH`), and the metric lookup all read from it. `is_write_op` and the `metric_op` strcmp chain are deleted.
- **Add** `MetricOp` values + `op_names` labels for the five missing ops so each gets its own `by_op` counter.

## Auth semantics preserved
The check order (write-token → read-only-replica → rate-limit → global-ns → snapshot-write-token) matches the previous flow exactly. The full auth / token-admin / rate-limit / snapshot / multitenancy contract suite passes unchanged.

## Downstream (no edits needed)
The Prometheus exporter iterates `by_op.items()` dynamically and the Grafana panel keys on `{{op}}`, so the five new counters surface automatically.

## Verification
- Live check confirmed history/export/consolidate/forget/purge each increment their own counter with `by_op.other == 0`.
- Added a contract regression check asserting the five ops advance their own counter and no longer inflate `by_op.other`.
- Builds **0-warning under gcc `-Werror`**; `make check` passes. clang / ASan / UBSan / TSan / CMake run in CI.

Closes #187

items.title: alternator: add even more vector search features
items.body:
This series continues to implement features of Alternator vector search which have not yet implemented. 

The main feature added in this series is **pre-filtering** (filter passed to vector store), using `KeyConditionExpression`. Currently, the vector store only has access to the base table's **key** columns, so only those can be used in pre-filtering. In a later, separate, pull request (#29959) we will add the ability to _project_ additional columns into the vector store and use those in pre-filtering.

Additional smaller improvements included in this series:

* Additional tests for already existing Alternator vector search features.
* Cap the "Limit" of a vector-search Query to 1000. This is the same limit that is enforced in CQL vector-search.
* Fix some metrics whose per-table versions we forgot to update.

We've decided not to backport improvements to the Alternator vector search feature, so do not backport this one either.

items.title: fix: populate network_events table from /metrics endpoint
items.body:
Closes the Day 2 gap Devansh caught during pipeline verification.

## What was wrong
The `network_events` Postgres table was defined on Day 2 but no code ever wrote to it. The `/metrics` endpoint was writing only to InfluxDB. Verified via `grep -rn "network_events"` - only hit was the model definition itself.

## What changed
`/metrics` now writes to BOTH InfluxDB (time-series) AND Postgres `network_events` (structured event log), matching the architecture doc Layer 2.

## How it works
1. Build the InfluxDB Point (unchanged)
2. Write to InfluxDB - if this fails, return 500 (same as before)
3. Build a NetworkEvent ORM object from the same fields
4. Insert into Postgres via async session
5. If Postgres write fails, log a warning and continue - InfluxDB write already succeeded so we don't fail the whole request

Response now includes status of both writes for visibility:
```json
{"status":"written","influxdb":"written","postgres":"written"}
```

## How to verify
docker compose up -d

uvicorn app.main:app --reload    # in backend/
Send a test packet
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/metrics 

-H "Content-Type: application/json" 

-d '{"src_ip":"192.168.1.10","dst_ip":"192.168.1.20","src_port":54321,"dst_port":443,"protocol":"TCP","packet_length":1500,"timestamp":"2026-06-16T10:00:00Z"}'
Check Postgres
docker exec -it infra-postgres-1 psql -U dev -d appdb -c "SELECT * FROM network_events ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 5;"

Verified locally - row landed in Postgres correctly with auto-generated `captured_at` timestamp.

## Note
Pair-fixed with the team in person (Devansh flagged the empty table after his end-to-end pipeline validation). Reviewer should be someone who didn't pair-write this.
